title: Alfredo Jaar Is Still Trying to Change the World
summary: Four decades after his Times Square artwork challenged the definition of America, the Chilean architect calls himself “a pessimist with my intellect and an optimist with my will.”

title: Another Abstract Public Artwork Faces Trump’s Senseless Ire
summary: The president wants to replace José de Rivera's “Infinity” (1967) outside the National Museum of American History with a statue of George Washington.

title: Member Event: ISCP Ground Floor Studio Visits
summary: ​Join us on September 30 for an evening of studio visits and conversations with the NYC-based artists selected for the International Studio & Curatorial Program's Ground Floor Residency.

title: James McNeill Whistler’s Music for the Eyes
summary: A long-awaited Whistler retrospective at Tate Britain makes the case that every brushstroke, color, and omission serves the pursuit of harmony.

summary: “We The Youth” (1987), painted on a wall co-owned by a real-estate developer, could become the city’s first outdoor mural on the Philadelphia Register of Historic Places.

title: A Twisted Sculpture Lands on Manhattan's High Line
summary: The inflatable cavatappi-shaped artwork, inspired by fashion house Bulgari’s serpent motif, will remain on view through New York Fashion Week.

title: Madelon Vriesendorp’s Subconscious Cities
summary: An exhibition explores the creativity and imagination of an artist whose way of seeing influences architects and artists.

title: Activists Protest Bayeux Tapestry Sponsor’s Ties to Israeli Settlements
summary: Demonstrators at the British Museum decried billionaire Igor Tulchinsky’s financing of a community center in an illegal Israeli settlement in the Occupied West Bank.

title: Europe’s Art Theft Problem Is Much Bigger Than the Louvre
summary: A wave of museum thefts is exposing the vulnerabilities of institutions struggling to protect irreplaceable collections after years of underfunding.

title: Six Decades of David Hockney on View in Gloucester, MA
summary: “Hockney Reproduction(s)" explores the artist's innovation through reproductive media at the Manship Artists Residency. Opens September 11, 2026

title: Good Muslim Artist, Bad Muslim Artist

title: The Battle of New York

title: Brooklyn, Say Hello to Your First Craft Supply Library
summary: Crochet hooks, thermal laminators, and button makers are among the 31 items now available to rent from the Brooklyn Public Library’s new lending program.
